newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Tuesday and traders said a technical correction on the domestic A share markets kept repo rates largely at Monday's level.
Tha annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose slightly to 13.10 percent from 13.01 percent on Monday.
Turnover was very heavy at 13.51 million lots from 10.95 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Shanghai's A share index fell by 1.76 percent on Monday on a technical correction after surges in the past few days. Its Shenzhen counterpart shed 0.79 percent.
Traders said the correction prevented institutions from borrowing new funds on the repo markets.
They believe the rates will continue to be affected by the A markets' performance in the next few days. "If the A markets recover, the rates will go up correspondingly," said a trader.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up for the third straight day on Tuesday but traders said the contracts seemed to have approached resistance levels and would find it hard to to go up further for the rest of this week.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 117.33 yuan from 117.00 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 2.72 million lots from 1.69 million.
"The 10-year bond will shortly meet resistance after ending well above the 117-yuan level today," said one trader. "The market is likely to move around current levels for the rest of this week."
